name: Tevul Yom (Immersed That Day — Detailed Laws)
notes: The existing 'tevul_yom' entry is minimal; this tractate covers the full halakhic status of the tevul yom — their degree of impurity (third grade), what they disqualify vs. render impure, and how they interact with terumah, hullin, and kodashim.

name: Connection of Foods (Chibbur/Tziruf) for Impurity Purposes
notes: Whether foods stuck together, batter-cakes joined in baking, froth, scum, or liquids floating on other liquids serve as connectives (mitzaref/mechubar) for purposes of transmitting impurity from a tevul yom or other impure sources.

name: Nitzok (Stream of Poured Liquid as Connective)
notes: Whether a stream of liquid poured from one vessel to another serves as a connective for transmitting impurity between them; discussed in context of tevul yom touching the stream.

name: Yad (Handle) of Food for Impurity
notes: Handles or stems of food that serve as connectives for impurity transmission — when the handle is touched by an impure person or tevul yom, whether the food itself becomes impure.

name: Ashkelon Grappling-Irons and Broken Tool Susceptibility
notes: Whether broken tools (Ashkelon grappling-irons, pitchforks, rakes, combs) that retain partial functionality remain susceptible to impurity; includes the rabbinic principle introduced by the scribes referenced by Rabbi Joshua.

name: Court Stipulation in Terumah Separation (Tenai Beit Din)
notes: The court-established stipulation that if terumah separated under a condition (e.g., 'if it comes up safely') breaks before reaching the cistern, it does not retroactively subject the cistern contents to terumah restrictions.

name: Third-Degree Impurity Clean in Hullin (Shlishi b'Hullin Tahor)
notes: The principle that an item with third-degree impurity is considered clean with respect to non-sacred (hullin) food, though it disqualifies terumah; central to Tractate Tevul Yom chapters 3-4.

name: Liquids Issuing from an Impure Person
notes: Whether liquids that issue from or are touched by an impure person (including tevul yom) acquire first-degree impurity and can render other things susceptible to impurity; dispute between Rabbi Meir and the Sages regarding tevul yom.

name: Get Written for One Departing on Dangerous Journey
hebrew: גט לאדם היוצא בשיירה או בספינה
notes: The rabbinic enactment allowing a get to be written for a man being led to execution or departing on a dangerous sea voyage or caravan journey, even before separation occurs; later extended to the dangerously ill.

name: Conditional Separation of Terumah
notes: Separating terumah subject to a condition (e.g., 'let this be terumah if it comes up safely' or 'let this be terumah of tithe after nightfall'); whether such conditional designations take effect.
